## Position Overview
We are looking for a skilled and detail-oriented ICT Systems Test Engineer to join our team and play a critical role in ensuring the quality, reliability, and performance of our technology systems. The successful candidate will be responsible for designing and executing comprehensive test strategies, identifying defects, and working collaboratively with development and infrastructure teams to deliver robust, high-quality solutions. This role suits a methodical and analytical professional with a strong technical background in software and systems testing, a commitment to quality assurance best practices, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, agile environment.
## Key Responsibilities
- Specify, develop, and execute detailed test plans, test scripts, and test cases to validate the behaviour, functionality, and integrity of ICT systems across multiple platforms and environments.
- Identify, diagnose, and document functionality errors and faults in systems and programming code within established testing protocols, quality standards, and compliance guidelines to ensure systems perform to specification.
- Design and conduct regression, integration, performance, and user acceptance testing (UAT) to ensure new and updated systems meet defined requirements and business needs.
- Utilise automated test software and frameworks to streamline testing processes, improve test coverage, and increase efficiency across the software development lifecycle.
- Produce clear and comprehensive defect reports, test summary reports, and related quality assurance documentation, ensuring traceability from requirements through to test outcomes.
- Perform systems architecture reviews and assessments, evaluating current and future hardware and software configurations, and contributing recommendations to inform strategic technical direction.
- Collaborate closely with software developers, business analysts, and project managers to clarify requirements, resolve defects, and support timely delivery of system releases.
- Create, review, and maintain technical documentation including procedural guides, operational manuals, instructional materials, technical specifications, and maintenance inventory records.
- Analyse test results and defect trends to identify recurring issues, recommend process improvements, and support continuous quality improvement initiatives across the organisation.
- Participate in agile ceremonies such as sprint planning, stand-ups, and retrospectives, contributing a quality assurance perspective throughout the development cycle.
- Assess risks associated with system changes and releases, providing input into risk mitigation strategies and supporting informed decision-making across project and operational teams.
- Support the evaluation, selection, and implementation of testing tools, methodologies, and frameworks to ensure the organisation's testing capabilities remain current and effective.
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- A bachelor's degree or higher in Information Technology, Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
- Demonstrated experience in ICT systems testing, quality assurance, or a closely related technical role, with a solid understanding of the software development and systems engineering lifecycle.
- Proficiency in writing and executing test plans, test cases, and test scripts across functional, non-functional, and regression testing scenarios.
- Hands-on experience with test automation tools and frameworks such as Selenium, Cypress, JUnit, TestNG, or comparable technologies.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to diagnose complex system faults and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
- Experience producing high-quality technical documentation, including test reports, defect logs, operational guides, and system specifications.
- Familiarity with agile and DevOps methodologies and the ability to integrate quality assurance activities into iterative development workflows.
- Solid understanding of systems architecture, network infrastructure, and software integration concepts relevant to enterprise ICT environments.
- Competency with defect tracking and test management tools such as JIRA, Azure DevOps, Zephyr, or similar platforms.
- Excellent communication, collaboration, and organisational skills, with a strong commitment to delivering quality outcomes within agreed timeframes.
## Preferred Qualifications
- ISTQB certification (Foundation Level or above) or an equivalent recognised qualification in software testing or quality assurance.
- Experience working in regulated industries or environments with strict compliance, security, or governance requirements, such as government, finance, or healthcare.
- Exposure to performance and load testing tools such as Apache JMeter, LoadRunner, or Gatling.
- Familiarity with cybersecurity testing principles, including vulnerability assessments and secure coding practices.
- Experience with cloud-based environments and platforms such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud, and an understanding of how they impact testing strategies.
- Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines and associated tools such as Jenkins, GitLab CI, or Bamboo.
- A postgraduate qualification or additional certifications in project management, IT governance, or related fields, such as ITIL or PRINCE2, would be highly regarded.
## Why Join Us?
- Be part of a collaborative, inclusive, and forward-thinking team that values technical excellence and continuous improvement, where your contributions directly shape the quality of systems used across the organisation.
- Access ongoing professional development opportunities, including support for industry certifications, training programmes, and attendance at relevant conferences and events.
- Enjoy a flexible working environment with options for hybrid work arrangements, supporting a healthy work-life balance without compromising on career growth.
- Work on complex, large-scale ICT projects that offer genuine variety and the opportunity to deepen your expertise across diverse technologies and industries.
- Receive a competitive remuneration package with a clear pathway for career progression within a growing organisation that invests in its people.
## Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Super

Costa is seeking expressions of interest from jobseekers for up to 50 full-time ongoing Citrus Harvest, Packing and Farm Worker roles in the Renmark, SA and the broader Riverland region, to support our citrus operations.
Our peak intake period is generally from March to June. A further intake is generally available around July/August, depending on crop timing, weather, market demand and operational requirements. As a large citrus operation, some full-time ongoing roles may be available year-round, commencing at different times during the season depending on business needs.

About the roles
Available roles may include citrus picking, thinning, packing, crop care, general farm labouring, quality control, cleaning, housekeeping, stacking cartons, container loading, receivals, despatch, basic harvest recording, production reporting, farm and harvest administration and other general farming, harvest, packhouse or administration duties as directed by a supervisor or leading hand.
Farm and harvest roles are physically demanding and may involve standing or walking for extended periods, repetitive movement, frequent ladder climbing, bending, squatting, lifting, carrying and working outdoors in varying weather conditions. Workers may be required to lift or carry items up to approximately 20kg.
Packhouse roles may include stacking cartons on the box-line, pre-packs, auto-packers, floor general duties, container loading, computer pack, receivals, despatch, quality control, reporting, cleaning and other packing duties as required.
Cleaning roles may include cleaning offices, packhouse areas, accommodation facilities and other work areas.
Administration roles may include a variety of manual and computer-based clerical duties, including document processing, reconciliations, reception and general office support.
Some higher-level roles may also be available depending on business needs, including tractor, truck and forklift operator roles, quality control roles, team leader roles, assistant supervisor roles and supervisor roles. Applicants must hold any licence or permit legally required for the equipment being operated.

Hours of work
Full-time ongoing roles will be 38 ordinary hours per week, or the equivalent ordinary hours under the applicable roster arrangements, in accordance with the applicable industrial instrument.
Hours and work locations may vary depending on crop timing, weather, market demand, packhouse requirements and operational needs. Roles may involve early starts, late finishes, weekdays, weekends and public holidays, and may include afternoon or evening shift work during peak periods.
Work is located on rural properties, packhouse facilities and office locations in and around Renmark, South Australia and the broader Riverland region, including surrounding areas such as Murtho, Paringa, Pike Creek, Loxton and Lindsay Point. Applicants must be able to reliably travel to and from rostered work locations.

Pay and conditions
Pay and conditions will be in accordance with the applicable industrial instrument and the National Employment Standards:
Picking, harvest, crop care and farm work will be paid in accordance with the Horticulture Award 2020.
Packhouse work will be paid in accordance with the Vitor Citrus Packhouse Agreement 2024.
Administration and clerical work will be paid in accordance with the Clerks Private Sector Award 2020.
For picking, harvest, crop care and farm work, entry-level adult full-time roles may commence from the current Horticulture Award Level 1 full-time rate of $25.74 per hour, where Level 1 applies. Level 1 applies only where appropriate under the Award, including for workers who are new to the horticulture industry or have less than 3 months’ horticulture industry experience.
Workers performing picking, harvest, crop care or farm work who have 3 months or more horticulture industry experience will be classified and paid at least Horticulture Award Level 2, currently $26.44 per hour for adult full-time employees, or a higher classification where required based on the duties performed, skills, training, experience and applicable Award classification.
For packhouse work, entry-level adult full-time roles may commence from the current Vitor Citrus Packhouse Agreement 2024 Level 1 full-time rate of $25.79 per hour, where Level 1 applies. Level 2 movement provisions also apply under the Agreement. Workers classified at Level 2 under the Vitor Citrus Packhouse Agreement 2024 are currently paid $26.50 per hour for adult full-time employees.
Picking, packing, crop care, cleaning, administration and general labouring roles are generally classified based on the duties performed, the applicable industrial instrument, training, experience and demonstrated competency.
Tractor, truck and forklift operator roles are generally classified at Level 2, Level 3 or Level 4, depending on the duties performed, equipment operated, required licence, training and competency.
Team leader, assistant supervisor and supervisor roles may be classified at higher levels depending on the duties performed, team size, level of responsibility, training, experience and demonstrated competency.
Some citrus picking work may be paid by piece rate. Where piece rates apply, pieceworkers will receive a piecework record before commencing the piecework task. A minimum pay rate guarantee will apply in accordance with the Horticulture Award 2020, and pieceworkers will be paid at least the applicable minimum wage guarantee for their classification and hours worked.
Packhouse and administration roles are generally paid on an hourly basis in accordance with the applicable industrial instrument.
Superannuation and any applicable overtime, penalty rates, allowances and loadings will be paid in accordance with the applicable industrial instrument.

Training and development
Previous horticulture, packhouse or administration experience is not required for entry-level roles. Costa provides workplace induction, safety training and task-specific training.
There may be opportunities to develop further skills, including machinery competency, forklift training, truck licensing, first aid training, administration skills or leadership development, depending on business needs, role availability, performance, attendance and suitability.

About you
To be successful, applicants should:
Be willing and able to perform physically demanding work where required
Be reliable, punctual and safety-focused
Be able to follow instructions and safe work procedures
Be willing to work rostered shifts, including weekends and public holidays where required
Be willing and able to complete picking, packing, crop work, packhouse work, cleaning, administration or general labouring duties
Have good fine and gross motor skills
Work respectfully and cooperatively in a multicultural team environment
Have good attention to detail and a positive attitude
Be available for ongoing full-time employment
Be able to reliably travel to and from rural worksites, packhouse facilities and/or office locations
Hold valid working rights in Australia

How to apply
If you are interested in future full-time ongoing Citrus Harvest, Farm, Packhouse or Administration opportunities with Costa in the Renmark and Riverland region, please submit your expression of interest through the link below.

https://costagroup.currentjobs.co/Job/Farm-and-Harvest-Workers-Riverland-Full-time-LMT-2026-27/Riverland-Region/3098

Shortlisted applicants will be contacted by email or phone as suitable roles become available. Applicants will be required to provide evidence of their right to work during the application process.

## Position Overview
We are looking for a skilled and detail-oriented Database Administrator to join our team and take ownership of the design, implementation, and ongoing management of our database systems. The successful candidate will play a critical role in ensuring the integrity, security, and performance of organisational data assets. This role suits a proactive and technically proficient professional with a strong background in database management and a commitment to delivering reliable, high-quality data infrastructure. Experience working within a collaborative IT environment and the ability to communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders will be highly regarded.
## Key Responsibilities
- Design, develop, and maintain database architecture, data structures, tables, and naming conventions to ensure the accuracy, consistency, and completeness of all data master files
- Establish, monitor, and maintain backup and recovery procedures, ensuring business continuity and minimal disruption in the event of a system failure
- Implement and enforce database security protocols, integrity controls, and access management policies to safeguard sensitive organisational data
- Administer and maintain comprehensive database documentation, including guidelines, policies, and operational procedures, ensuring these remain current and fit for purpose
- Plan and perform database upgrades, patches, and migrations, including thorough testing, debugging, and issue resolution in accordance with approved quality assurance processes
- Monitor database performance on an ongoing basis, identifying bottlenecks and implementing tuning, indexing, and optimisation strategies to maximise efficiency
- Collaborate with developers, systems analysts, and business stakeholders to translate data requirements into effective and scalable database solutions
- Analyse existing database systems and workflows, recommending and implementing improvements to enhance reliability, performance, and maintainability
- Provide technical support and troubleshooting assistance for database-related incidents, working to resolve issues promptly and minimise operational impact
- Ensure database environments comply with relevant data governance frameworks, privacy legislation, and organisational standards, including alignment with Australian Privacy Principles where applicable
- Assist in capacity planning activities by assessing current usage trends and forecasting future storage and performance requirements
- Support the development and maintenance of data integration processes, including ETL pipelines and data warehouse environments, in collaboration with cross-functional teams
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience
- Demonstrated experience in a Database Administrator or similar role, with hands-on responsibility for managing enterprise-level database environments
- Proficiency in one or more leading relational database management systems, such as Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL, or PostgreSQL
- Strong working knowledge of SQL, including query writing, stored procedures, functions, and performance tuning
- Experience designing and implementing backup, recovery, and disaster recovery strategies in production environments
- Solid understanding of database security principles, including user access controls, encryption, and audit logging
- Ability to diagnose and resolve complex database performance issues through monitoring tools, execution plans, and indexing strategies
- Familiarity with data modelling techniques and the ability to translate business requirements into well-structured database designs
- Sound understanding of IT service management practices and experience working within structured change management processes
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a methodical approach to troubleshooting
- Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to liaise confidently with both technical teams and business stakeholders
## Preferred Qualifications
- Relevant vendor certifications such as Microsoft Certified: Azure Database Administrator Associate, Oracle Database Administrator Certified Professional, or equivalent
- Experience with cloud-based database platforms, including Azure SQL, Amazon RDS, or Google Cloud SQL
- Exposure to NoSQL database technologies such as MongoDB, Cassandra, or Redis
- Experience in data warehousing environments and familiarity with ETL tools and processes
- Knowledge of scripting languages such as PowerShell, Python, or Bash for automation of routine database tasks
- Familiarity with DevOps practices and experience working within Agile or ITIL-aligned environments
- Prior experience in a regulated industry such as finance, healthcare, or government, with an understanding of associated compliance obligations
## Why Join Us?
- Be part of a supportive and collaborative team culture that values continuous learning, knowledge sharing, and professional development
- Access ongoing training opportunities, certification support, and clear pathways for career progression within a growing technology function
- Enjoy flexible working arrangements, including hybrid work options, to support a healthy work-life balance
- Work on meaningful, complex data challenges that have a genuine impact across the organisation
- Receive a competitive remuneration package with additional benefits including superannuation, annual leave loading, and access to an employee wellbeing programme

Mechanical Fitter/Fitter – Full-Time
Location:  Welshpool Western Australia 6106
Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: $80,000 – $110,000 per annum (depending on skills and experience)

MINPROVISE INTERNATIONALPTY LTD is a leading total solutions provider delivering specialist maintenance and shutdown services, engineering, fabrication, project services, and sustaining capital works. We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

We are currently seeking experienced and motivated Fitters to join our growing team on a full-time basis.

About the Role
As a Fitter, you will be responsible for assembling, installing, maintaining, and repairing a wide range of mechanical equipment and machinery. You will work closely with engineers and maintenance teams to ensure equipment operates safely, efficiently, and in accordance with industry standards.

Key Responsibilities
•	Read and interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, and technical specifications.
•	Assemble, install, and commission mechanical equipment and components.
•	Carry out preventative maintenance and routine servicing of machinery.
•	Diagnose mechanical faults and perform repairs or replace defective components.
•	Use fabrication equipment and welding techniques to modify or manufacture components where required.
•	Ensure the correct alignment, calibration, and adjustment of machinery and equipment.
•	Conduct inspections and testing to ensure compliance with quality and safety standards.
•	Safely operate hand tools, power tools, and workshop machinery.
•	Maintain accurate records of maintenance, repairs, and equipment servicing.
•	Collaborate with engineers, supervisors, and other tradespeople to complete projects efficiently.
•	Assist with training apprentices and junior team members when required.
•	Follow all workplace health and safety policies and procedures.

Skills and Experience
•	Minimum 1–2 years of full-time experience as a Fitter or in a similar mechanical fitting role.
•	Ability to read and interpret technical drawings and specifications.
•	Strong troubleshooting and mechanical problem-solving skills.
•	Experience using mechanical fitting tools, workshop equipment, and fabrication machinery.
•	Strong commitment to workplace safety and quality workmanship.
•	Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
•	Excellent communication and organisational skills.

What We Offer
•	Full-time, permanent employment.
•	Competitive salary of $80,000 – $110,000 per annum.
•	Opportunities to work on major mining and industrial projects.
•	Ongoing training and career development.
•	Supportive team environment with long-term career opportunities

We are currently seeking experienced and motivated Boilermakers to join our growing team on a full-time basis.
About the Role

As a Boilermaker, you will be responsible for fabricating, assembling, installing, maintaining, and repairing structural steel, pressure vessels, heavy equipment, and metal components used in mining, industrial, and construction projects. You will work closely with engineers, supervisors, and maintenance teams to ensure all fabrication and welding work is completed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with engineering specifications and Australian Standards.

Key Responsibilities
•	Read and interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, fabrication plans, and technical specifications.
•	Fabricate, assemble, install, and repair structural steel, heavy machinery components, tanks, chutes, hoppers, conveyors, and other metal 
structures.
•	Mark out, cut, shape, bend, and prepare metal materials using fabrication equipment.
•	Perform welding using MIG, TIG, Stick, and Flux-Cored Arc Welding (FCAW) processes as required.
•	Carry out maintenance and repairs on plant and mining equipment during shutdowns and ongoing operations.
•	Inspect fabricated and welded components to ensure compliance with quality standards and engineering specifications.
•	Safely operate welding equipment, hand tools, power tools, cranes, hoists, and workshop machinery.
•	Identify faults, perform modifications, and recommend repair solutions where required.
•	Maintain accurate records of fabrication, repairs, inspections, and completed work.
•	Work collaboratively with engineers, supervisors, and other tradespeople to complete projects on time.
•	Assist with training apprentices and junior team members where required.
•	Follow all workplace health and safety policies, procedures, and site regulations.

•	Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and fabrication specifications.
•	Strong welding, fabrication, and metalworking skills.
•	Experience working with structural steel, heavy equipment, and industrial or mining plant.
•	Ability to safely operate fabrication machinery, welding equipment, and workshop tools.
•	Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving abilities.
•	Excellent attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship.
•	Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced environment.

What We Offer
•	Full-time, permanent employment.
•	Competitive salary of $80,000 – $110,000 per annum.
•	Opportunities to work on major mining, shutdown, and industrial projects.
•	Ongoing training and career development.
•	Supportive team environment with long-term career opportunities.
